13_marg737: RABANUS. It is read, or it is written: they declare that this book is found nowhere, like the book of the wars of the Lord, of which mention is made in the book of Numbers, and the songs of Solomon and his discourses on the nature of trees, herbs, beasts, birds, creeping things and fishes. Or what is said in the book of the Chronicles: "Now the rest of the acts of Solomon, first and last, are written in the books of Nathan the prophet, and of Ahias the Silonite, and in the vision of Addo the seer against Jeroboam the son of Nabat," and many volumes of this kind, which it proves were written but which it is certain do not exist today. For when Judea was laid waste by the Chaldeans, the library was consumed by the enemy's fire. But a few books were repaired or restored by Esdras the high priest, through the diligence of prophecy. This Esdras was a scribe in the law of God, who devised readier shapes of letters than the Hebrews had had until then. And there are some who say that the Book of the Just is the Book of Kings, in which are contained the just prophets Samuel, Gad and Nathan, in which it is written how Saul, departing from the fear of the Lord, perished through disobedience.

13_marg742: David, king and prophet, who did not return evil to his persecutors, when Saul and Jonathan had fallen in battle, cursed the mountains of Gelboe in his lamentation: Ye mountains of Gelboe, let neither dew nor rain etc. What fault did the mountains commit? But because Gelboe is interpreted 'a running down', and through Saul, anointed and dead, the anointing and death of our mediator is expressed, by Gelboe are fittingly signified the proud hearts of the Jews, which, while they flow away in the desires of this world, mixed themselves in the death of the anointed, that is, of Christ. And because in them the anointed king dies in time, they are dried up from all dew of grace. Of them it is said that they cannot be fields of firstfruits. For the proud mountains of the Hebrews do not bear the first fruits, since at the Redeemer's coming they for the most part remained in unbelief and would not follow the beginnings of the faith. For holy Church, made fruitful in her firstfruits by the multitude of the gentiles, scarcely at the end of the world receives the Jews whom she finds, and gathering the last ones lays them up as the remnants of the harvest. Whence: THE REMNANT OF ISRAEL SHALL BE SAVED. Yet the mountains of Gelboe can be cursed by the prophet's mouth, so that, while the fruit dies as the earth dries up, the possessors of the land might be struck with the loss of barrenness, that they themselves might receive the sentence of the curse who, as their iniquity required, had deserved to have the death of the king take place among them.
13_marg743: Blood and fat give strength to the body. So those by whom Saul and Jonathan were slain gave strength to their subjects, as though [they had been slain] not by rustics. Or thus: Saul was rejected by God, and basely slain by the uncircumcised, as though he were not anointed with oil, because of the blood of the slain, namely of the seventy-five priests who burned fat to the Lord, whom Saul ordered to be killed though innocent.
13_marg744: THE ARROW OF JONATHAN etc. and THE SWORD OF SAUL etc. He shows that Jonathan and Saul were warlike and most valiant, and praises in them the comeliness of their form and the constancy of their mind.
13_marg745: Allegorically. First the prophet David figuratively bewails Saul and Jonathan, who, though they were mighty and always prevailed over their enemies, being wounded and struck down in the midst of the battle, fell. So also Christians bewail those who, fighting against the demons, slip in the slipperiness of the world (for Gelboe is interpreted 'slippery mountains'), and, giving up the hope of recovery, kill themselves with their own blade of despair, as Saul did falling upon his sword. But the Philistines, that is, the demons, carrying off the spoils of virtues from the slain, ascribe the victory to their own strength, since such things befall the just by the promise of God. But our David in his elect groans at the fall of those who fall, and forbids it to be published in the cities of the aliens, that is, he commands the faithful to guard themselves warily, that they may have the shield of faith, the breastplate of justice, the helmet of salvation, and the sword of the spirit, which is the word of God, with which they may resist their adversaries, lest, shamefully overcome again, they give joy to their enemies.

13_marg746: RABANUS. The going up of David with his two wives into Hebron signifies 'the calling together of two peoples into the catholic Church'. For Hebron is interpreted 'marriage'. And the Church alone is the bride of the heavenly king. Thither David led every man with his household, because each of the faithful is called into that fellowship through the preaching of the gospel, where there is no distinction of Jew and Greek.
13_marg747: RABANUS. Because, while the proud and contemptuous spurn the grace of God, the elect, by the fame of preaching and the pursuit of virtues, confess that Christ is king among his people, to whom has been given "all power in heaven and on earth."

13_marg751: RABANUS. It is well said that David reigned seven days [so the edition] and six months in Hebron, which is interpreted 'marriage' or 'everlasting vision', because Christ reigns in the Church, which is his person, through the whole time of this life, which runs its course in the sevenfold number of days, according to that: "Behold I am with you all days, even to the consummation of the world"; and because after the fulfilment of the six, that is, the perfection of good work, he leads his elect to the true sabbath, that is, the everlasting rest, where they shall enjoy the perpetual vision of God. Now Hebron is a city in the tribe of Juda which was once called Arbe, although in the Greek manuscripts it is wrongly given as Arboc, as also in ours, whereas in the Hebrew it is read Arbe, that is, 'four', because Abraham and Isaac and Jacob were buried there, and the great Adam, although some suppose he [was buried] in the place of Calvary. This was once the metropolis of the Philistines and the dwelling of the giants, afterwards a priestly city and [a city] of refuge. It lies on the southern side, about twenty-two miles from Aelia, where the oak of Abraham, which is also the terebinth, which is also Mambre, was shown until the reign of the emperor Constantine, and his mausoleum [is seen] at the present time. And though a church has now been built there by our people, the place of the terebinth is worshipped round about by all the nations with superstition, because under it Abraham received the angels as guests. It was first called Arbe, afterwards Hebron, from one of the sons of Caleb; and it was founded seven years before Tanis, the city of Egypt.
13_marg752: AND ABNER WENT OUT etc. RABANUS. Josephus explains this passage thus: Abner moved forward a very choice army, to engage with the tribe of Juda. For he was angry against those by whom David had been ordained king. Against him came Joab, sent by David, the son of Sarvia his sister; he was set as captain of the host against Abner. With him were his brothers Abisai and Asael and all David's armed men; and coming to a certain spring in the city of Gabaon, he drew up his line for battle. And when Abner said to him that he wished to test which of them had the stronger army, it was agreed between both that they should send twelve men to fight; and when the swords were drawn, David's men, holding the heads of the enemy, pierced their loins and sides with their swords, until all perished as if in one appointed danger. When these fell, the rest of the army also gave way, and Abner's people were beaten. And Joab did not cease to pursue the fleeing, commanding the armed men to hasten and not to slacken in killing. His brothers also fought most readily; among whom Asael was the more renowned, who had such glory in swiftness of foot that he outran even horses in running. He pursued Abner, turning aside to neither side.
13_marg753: AND ABNER SAID TO JOAB etc. Abner, of the tribe of Benjamin, captain of Saul's army, provoked the young men of David to battle; and Saul, not yet an apostle, of the tribe of Benjamin, a Pharisee, provoked the apostles to the contest, and was present at the killing of Stephen.
13_marg754: NOW ASAEL etc. GREGORY. Asael signifies those whom vehement fury seizes and drives headlong. They are to be avoided the more cautiously in that same onset of fury, the more madly they are carried away. Whence Abner, that is, 'lamp of the father', flees, because the tongue of teachers, which shows forth the heavenly light of God, when it sees anyone's mind carried along the steep places of fury, refrains from returning the darts of words against the angry man, as if unwilling to strike the pursuer. But when the wrathful are mitigated by no consideration, and like Asael do not cease to pursue, it is necessary that those who try to restrain the furious should not rouse themselves to fury, but show whatever there is of calm; and some things they should put forward subtly, by which they may obliquely pierce the mind of the furious man. Whence Abner pierced his pursuer not with the point but with the butt of the spear. For to strike with the point is to oppose with the onset of open rebuke; but to strike with the butt of the spear is to touch the furious man calmly with certain things, and as it were to overcome him by sparing him. And Asael at once falls, because agitated minds, when they both feel themselves spared and yet are touched inwardly, under calm, by the reason of the answers, immediately fall from that to which they had raised themselves. Because, therefore, struck by gentleness they spring back from the onset of their fury, they die as it were without the steel.

13_marg756: THERE WAS A LONG [WAR]. RABANUS. The house of David is the heavenly Jerusalem, which partly is a pilgrim on earth, partly reigns with the Lord in heaven. But the house of Saul, the proud and wicked king, is Babylon, which makes all nations commit fornication. Between these there is a long war, because she who is according to the flesh persecutes her who is according to the spirit. But the house of David rejoices in the growth of her children even in persecution; the house of Saul fails in its iniquity, and at length, according to its deserts, will be sunk in the depth of the abyss.

13_marg759: ABNER ALSO SPOKE. RABANUS. Abner exhorts all Israel to leave Isboseth the son of Saul and come over to David, because the holy teachers, who are called lamp of the father, full of the light of faith and knowledge, exhort all nations to spurn the worship of idols, to leave the error of confusion together with its author the devil, and to hasten to come to the true David, that is, Christ. For Joab too, who, speaking to Abner in guile, struck him in the groin and killed him, signifies the ancient enemy, who subverts the faithful by fraud and kills them through the contagion of lust. For Joab is interpreted 'enemy' or likewise 'father'. For the devil is the head of all the wicked. Whence: "You are of your father the devil." Of this killing David is guiltless, because "God tempteth no man," who "will have all men to be saved." "But by the envy of the devil death came into the world." The person and name of Joab can also signify the people of the Jews, who were always enemies of the preachers and persecuted the faith of Christ everywhere.
